transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (AstralForge CTO), Samir Patel (SRE Lead), Hannah Lee (Product)

Summary (auto): high-level discovery on Dedicated/reserved capacity needs, isolation constraints, burst model and timeline. Customer wants predictable cost and a private/VPC path; worried about latency spikes during nightly jobs.

Topics: dedicated pool sizing; isolation (tenant fencing / single-tenant nodes); burst strategy and prewarm; KMS + logs; success criteria for POC.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intro, i'm maya chen, account exec on the dedicated team at Redwood. we've got diego from infra here too.
[00:08] Priya: hi, thanks, i'm priya, cto at astralforge, and that's samir our sre and hannah from product. appreciate the time.
[00:15] Diego: hey all — i'll be the technical badger today, walk through topology questions and perf tradeoffs.
[00:22] Hannah: great, really curious about how reserved nodes work — our primary ask is consistent latency under bursty load.
[00:30] Maya: perfect. a quick framing — we offer hosted, dedicated reserved pools, and private/VPC installs. sounds like you want dedicated reserved GPUs with some isolation for sensitive models and a burst path? correct me if i'm wrong.
[00:45] Priya: yeah that's right. we run three main inference workloads: 1) short chat-like responses (95% < 300 tokens), 2) longer document summarization (up to ~1k tokens), and 3) nightly batch reranks. daytime spike patterns are what we worry about.
[01:05] Samir: and we need to ensure that the rerank jobs don't starve the chat service — last month we saw p99s jump from 120ms to 900ms during a bad run.
[01:15] Diego: okay.. that aligns with what dedicated helps with. two quick questions: do you need strict single-tenant hardware, or is tenant-fencing (soft isolation) acceptable?
[01:24] Priya: maybe both? for our PII-sensitive models we'd prefer single-tenant nodes or private deploy, but for user-facing chat maybe a dedicated pool with strong tenant fencing would do.
[01:35] Maya: totally reasonable hybrid approach. Redwood Dedicated supports per-customer GPU pools that can be single-tenant, and we also have VPC/private control plane options for on-prem-like isolation.
[01:45] Hannah: when you say single-tenant, is that literally exclusive GPUs or just logical isolation?
[01:50] Diego: exclusive GPUs — the node is dedicated to your tenant, so you don't share kernels or cache. logical fencing is where multiple tenants share the same GPU but we enforce quotas, cgroups, and compute scheduling to limit interference. the trade is cost vs utilization.
[02:10] Priya: cost is a factor, we have budget constraints but can't compromise latency for the chat product. what does a typical pricing shape look like?
[02:18] Maya: i'll follow up with exact numbers but rough tiers: single-tenant reserved node (eg 4x A100 class) per-month commitments; dedicated shared-pool lower commit; and hybrid models where you reserve baseline and burst to hosted. we'll send a model with examples.
[02:34] Samir: about burst — how does the burst path work? do we rely on Redwood hosted as overflow or pre-warm extra nodes?
[02:41] Diego: two patterns: 1) warm pool / prewarm where you keep spare nodes in standby, cheap to prewarm if you keep memory/KV cache warm; 2) overflow routing to hosted instances which are multi-tenant but elastically available. both can be combined — baseline reserved for steady traffic, warm pool for frequent bursts, hosted fallback for rare extreme storms.
[03:02] Priya: how long to spin up a prewarm node? we've seen some startups claim 3–5 minutes which is too slow for chat spikes.
[03:10] Diego: depends on model and kv-cache priming. for smaller chat models we can prewarm in ~45–90 seconds if you keep the model on-disk and use quick kernel init; for large summarization models with big kv caches it can be a few minutes. that's why we recommend cache snapshots for fast warm-up.
[03:30] Hannah: you mentioned KV cache — last time our infra team called it KV cash in the notes, ha, so clarification appreciated.
[03:36] Samir: ha, yes, kv cache. how much memory do we need for our models? we have a mix of 16b and 70b distil variants.
[03:45] Diego: ok rough numbers: 16b-ish models with quantization fit comfortably on 80–100GB GPU memory; 70b variants are trickier — they need 120GB+ or sharded execution. if you intend to serve both, we should discuss node types and whether you want mixed-instance pools.
[04:05] Priya: we were thinking to start with 8 GPUs reserved for baseline for the chat and warm pool of 2 nodes for bursts, then scale to 16 over next quarter if traffic ramps.
[04:16] Maya: that sounds pragmatic. Diego, any concerns with that sizing given their workloads?
[04:20] Diego: sounds fine but i'd like to see token/sec and concurrency distributions. if your 95th is small but you have high concurrency, batching helps but can bump latency. for chat you typically want low-latency path with small batch sizes and reserved qps.
[04:37] Priya: we can share sample traces — is 95/99 p99 SLOs enough or do you want raw logs?
[04:43] Maya: 7-day traces with lat/req sizes and token counts is perfect. also note any night batch windows so we can propose scheduling or traffic shaping.
[04:52] Samir: one more big ask — audit logs and key management. we need KMS integration and per-request audit trails for SOC 2, plus SSO for team access.
[05:02] Diego: Redwood Dedicated supports KMS/HSM integrations and audit logging; for private installs we can integrate into your key management. for hosted fallbacks we can also configure customer-managed keys in some cases.
[05:15] Priya: good. how about model rollouts vs fallback? e.g., if a newer model regresses we need quick fallback to previous version without traffic interruption.
[05:24] Diego: our rollout features include canary routing by percentage, instant fallback to pinned versions, and automatic fallback policies if latency/err rates exceed thresholds. small note — sometimes the transcription says 'rollouts' as 'roll-outs' in docs.
[05:37] Hannah: haha. okay. can you also run a short perf test to show p50/p95/p99 on our 16b model? we can send a smaller payload to start.
[05:45] Diego: yes, we'll run a perf workshop — ideally with a sample inference docker or via test keys against a staging model. schedule a 90-minute session and we'll bring profiling.
[05:55] Priya: timeline — we want a pilot within 3 weeks and production reserve in 8–10 weeks if the POC looks good. can you commit to that?
[06:05] Maya: yes that's a common cadence. SE perf workshop this week or next, then 2-week pilot, then contract.
[06:13] Samir: any gotchas on data residency? we have EU customers and need logs retained in-region.
[06:18] Diego: we support region-specific deployments and audit log retention policies. for strict residency you'd probably want a private/VPC control plane in EU or on-prem.
[06:27] Priya: ok, one objection — we've been evaluating Anthropic and some in-house infra. how do you compare on cost predictability?
[06:34] Maya: short answer: dedicated reserved nodes give predictable monthly cost and consistent tail latency; Anthropic hosted endpoints can be easier to start but unpredictable at scale. in-house gives control but ops burden. we'll include unit economics comparisons in the follow-up.
[06:48] Hannah: security team will want SOC 2 docs and possibly a security checklist. can you share that?
[06:53] Maya: yes will attach SOC 2, ISO summary, and our redwood-dedicated security checklist in the follow-up.
[07:00] Priya: any recommended fallback SLOs we should set for the POC?
[07:04] Diego: recommend p95 < 250ms for chat baseline, p99 < 700ms; for summarization don't set aggressive p99s — maybe p95 < 900ms. those are starting targets, we can adjust after perf runs.
[07:17] Priya: sounds reasonable.
[07:20] Maya: quick recap — action items: diego to size + cost, maya to send commercial and security docs, customer to share traces. perf workshop scheduled. any final questions?
[07:34] Samir: what's the expected SLA for dedicated vs hosted?
[07:37] Maya: dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets, hosted is standard best-effort with retention options; full details in the SOW.
[07:47] Hannah: ok thanks, we'll look for the email and get traces over asap.
[07:52] Priya: thanks everyone.
[07:55] Maya: thanks — we'll follow up with the pricing model + set the perf workshop. bye.

End of transcript.
